display.text:
poison log app

* create a Qt/QML 6.12 app in this directory. it should run on desktop linux initially.
* this app is used to allow the user to note on a map where they have applied herbicides/pesticides.
* the map should be a top down view of a piece of land, specified by address. there should be about 1 acre of land around the main structure visible.
* the user enters the address, and can position the area around the structure, then clicks ok, and the image of the land is stored.
* further operations on the map are done visually on the saved map, the map is fixed at that point.
* when the user is looking at the map, they can drag rectangles on the map (multiple rectangles).
* then they can enter some text in a text box to describe what was applied, how much, etc.
* the description has a date field, and a tag name, and a color to draw the rectangle as well.
* the user clicks "commit" and the info related to the rectangles and notes are stored in an sqlite database.
* on the main windows, there is also a list on the side that lists all the committed records, sorted by date, newest to oldest.
* selecting one of the records in the list displays the rectangles and notes on the map.
* if the user is in the middle of entering new rectangles and notes, those must be saved, even if the user clicks an item in the list.
* there is a button to resume editing after the user clicks away to view other notes.
* the application should always start showing the partially entered notes.
* there is a button to clear partially entered notes and discard them.

parts.text:
We have Qt Location with OSM plugin, WebEngine. Need to design.

Key design questions:
1. Map source: Qt Location OSM raster tiles. Need address geocoding. Qt Location's OSM plugin supports geocoding via Nominatim (QGeoServiceProvider geocoding). But Nominatim usage policy requires proper user agent; Qt's OSM plugin sets one? Should be fine for dev. Alternatively use manual lat/lon or address search via Nominatim REST. Use Qt Location Map with OSM plugin, geocode via QGeoCodingManager from osm plugin. For capturing fixed map image: Map.grabToImage(QQuickItemGrabResult) and save PNG. But Qt Location Map is a QQuickItem using scene graph; grabToImage should work for software renderer? Qt Location map renderer uses OpenGL scene graph; grabToImage of Map may return blank on some platforms. Alternative use WebEngine + Leaflet, but heavier and WebEngine grab is possible. Or fetch static map tiles ourselves and compose QImage (OSM tile server) — simple and reliable; plus a QML tile cache for interactive adjust? Hmm.

Requirement: interactive map to position area around structure, ~1 acre visible, then save image fixed. Need address search, drag map, then freeze.

Approach options:
A. Qt Location QML Map with OSM plugin + Map { gesture enabled } with fixed zoom computed for ~1 acre. Address search via Nominatim through QGeoCodingManager or REST. Capture with grabToImage. Rectangles drawn as QML overlays over saved image in edit mode; saved map is image. For committed records, store image path (map image shared per map). The "main" map is a single saved map? Text: "the image of the land is stored. further operations on the map are done visually on the saved map, the map is fixed". Likely one map/property? Could support multiple maps, but app scope: one saved map? Records tie to map image. Could design DB with maps table to support future multiple properties, but UI is single map. Maybe simpler: single map saved locally (map.png) + metadata. But database storing rectangles relative coords. Address specified by user at setup; perhaps allow reset map (dangerous). Plan should maybe ask.

B. Custom tile fetch in C++ + QML item rendering with QQuickPaintedItem. Overkill.

I lean Qt Location map for setup, capture via grabToImage (test). But Qt Location OSM geocoding may not work? Qt 6 OSM plugin supports geocoding. Let's check quickly whether plugin has geocoding (QGeoServiceProvider features). Could write test but read-only plan phase, can compile in /tmp? Plan mode forbids system changes? Read-only phase: shouldn't create files. We can inspect docs/plugins. No need.

Alternative robust: use Nominatim REST from QtNetwork for geocoding and OSM tile fetch using QNetworkAccessManager, compose map canvas via QML Canvas/Image tiles. More work and tile usage policy requires proper attribution/user agent. Static capture then straightforward. But interactive map can use QML Map. Actually grabbing interactive Map via grabToImage may fail on RHI; Qt Location has Map { } and MapItemView; use ShaderEffectSource? There is QQuickItem::grabToImage works with scene graph including OpenGL content? Historically grabToImage doesn't capture QtLocation Map reliably. Better save map by downloading tiles independently into QImage at chosen center/zoom, displayed as Image while adjusting too. This ensures exact saved image and easy fixed map. We could render tiles ourselves in QML using tile math with Repeater + Image from OSM URL, clipped. Then "capture" is compositing the tiles into PNG via C++. Simpler and avoids Qt Location dependency entirely; but more custom code for pan/zoom.

Actually can do map using Qt Location for interactive, then after OK store center/zoom and map image produced by a custom tile compositor (same tile coordinates) — consistent. But then why Qt Location? UI map during setup only, grab fallback. Could just display custom tile view with pan and zoom. Address geocoding via Nominatim REST. Custom tile view requires: lon/lat to tile x/y at zoom, show 3x3 or enough tiles for viewport, support panning, zoom level (fixed maybe 18/19), marker overlay. Capture: C++ fetch all tiles for viewport (slippy map) at request, composite at chosen pixel dimensions. Or capture from QML via grabbing the tile container QQuickItem whose children are Images — grabToImage works on Image items. A container Item with Image tiles and marker can grabToImage reliably. Then save PNG. That is simple.

Yet requirement "about 1 acre visible" - can compute pixels per meter from latitude and zoom. 1 acre = 4046.86 m², square ~63.6m. So viewport ~64m across. At zoom 19, resolution ~0.3m/px at equator, ~0.2m/px at lat 45; 64m => ~320px. Set map viewport e.g. 640x640 display showing ~64m => zoom chosen based on latitude and viewport. For "about 1 acre of land around the main structure visible", square viewport representing ~64m x 64m. We can set fixed ground width 70m and compute zoom. Display 600x600 px. On capture save image at maybe 1024x1024 by fetching higher zoom? Fixed image quality. Simpler save at displayed resolution 640x640 (tiles scaled). Good enough? Could capture at 2x resolution.

Panning custom slippy map is nontrivial but manageable: use QtLocation. Hmm.

Let's think of plan simplicity and risk. Qt Location Map + grabToImage simplest UI. We could test grab but plan only. We can note fallback.

Requirements:
- address entry, map preview, position area, OK saves image.
- Map fixed after save.
- Draw rectangles (multiple) by dragging on map.
- Enter text description, date field, tag name, color.
- Commit -> rectangles + notes stored in SQLite.
- Sidebar list of committed records, sorted newest first.
- Selecting record displays rectangles and notes.
- Draft rectangles/notes must persist even when clicking list item.
- Resume editing button.
- App always starts showing partially entered draft.
- Clear draft button.

Data model:
- map: one saved map (or maps table). Store image path, address, center lat/lon, zoom/ground size, capture resolution.
- records table: id, date, tag, color, notes, created_at.
- rectangles table: id, record_id (nullable for draft), x,y,w,h normalized 0..1 relative to image.
- draft singleton: either a draft record row with committed=0 plus rectangles; or separate draft table/JSON. Better unify: records table with status draft/committed. Draft record id maybe fixed 1. But list only committed. On commit, mark committed and create a new empty draft. Persist draft in DB so app restarts with it.

Since one map, rectangles are relative to map image. If map can be reset, records tied to map id. Add maps table for robustness even if UI single map. Perhaps overkill; but address change? The user likely can change map later? APP says image stored and fixed at that point. Could allow "Set up map" only if no map exists, and maybe a menu option to replace map (warn records). Plan could mention single property assumption and optional reset.

UI design:
Main window QML ApplicationWindow:
- Toolbar: address? once map set: "Map: address"; Resume editing button visible when viewing a committed record with existing draft; Clear draft; maybe New/Edit.
- Left/right sidebar: ListView records sorted date desc, each row tag/date/color swatch. Selecting sets viewedRecord; map displays that record's rectangles; editor fields show record (read-only?) or draft?
- Center: map image with rectangle overlays; edit rectangles only in draft/edit mode. "Resume editing" returns to draft.
- Editor panel: text area, date picker, tag field, color picker, Commit. When viewing a record: show record details (read-only), button "Resume editing" maybe; selecting record while draft in progress switches view but draft retained (auto-saved on every change).
- Draft autosave: QML field handlers update draft model and save (debounced) to DB; entering rectangles updates DB. Always persisted.
- Starting app: load draft (if rectangles/notes exist) and show it with edit mode. Else show map and empty draft edit.
- Selecting a list item while draft has content: save draft (already saved), switch to view record; top banner with "Resume editing".
- Clear draft: confirmation dialog, delete draft rectangles and clear fields; new empty draft.

# Implementation Plan: poison log

## Summary of decisions
- **Stack:** Qt 6.12.0 (`/home/dwight/Qt/6.12.0/gcc_64`), Qt Quick/QML, Qt SQL (SQLite), Qt Network. CMake + Ninja. No Qt Location dependency.
- **Map:** custom slippy-map canvas using OpenStreetMap raster tiles. Chosen over `QtLocation` so the visible map can be reliably captured to a fixed image, and so the tile source is pluggable for satellite imagery later.
- **Property scope:** one fixed property map, per APP.txt.
- **Draft persistence:** the draft is a real database row with `status='draft'`; all edits are written immediately, not held in QML memory.

## Project layout

```
CMakeLists.txt
src/
  main.cpp
  database.{h,cpp}          # connection, schema/migrations, transactions
  appstore.{h,cpp}          # application state, draft/commit/view commands
  recordlistmodel.{h,cpp}   # committed records, date DESC
  rectanglelistmodel.{h,cpp}# rectangles for draft or viewed record
  geocoder.{h,cpp}          # Nominatim search over QtNetwork
  tileimageprovider.{h,cpp} # async OSM tiles, UA, memory/disk cache
qml/
  Main.qml                  # window, sidebar, page switching
  MapSetupPage.qml          # address search + map positioning
  MapCanvas.qml             # tile rendering, drag-to-pan, crosshair
  MapView.qml               # fixed saved image + rectangle overlay
  RectangleEditor.qml       # draw/move/resize/delete rectangles
  RecordList.qml
  EditorPanel.qml           # draft form + commit/clear
  RecordDetails.qml         # read-only viewed record
tests/
  tst_database.cpp
  tst_appstore.cpp
```

## Database schema

```sql
map(
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(id = 1),
  address TEXT NOT NULL,
  center_lat REAL NOT NULL,
  center_lon REAL NOT NULL,
  ground_span_m REAL NOT NULL,
  image_path TEXT NOT NULL,
  image_width INTEGER NOT NULL,
  image_height INTEGER NOT NULL,
  attribution TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL
)

records(
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  map_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES map(id),
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('draft','committed')),
  date TEXT NOT NULL,             -- ISO YYYY-MM-DD
  tag TEXT NOT NULL,
  color TEXT NOT NULL,            -- #rrggbb
  notes TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
)

rectangles(
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  record_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES records(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  x REAL NOT NULL, y REAL NOT NULL,   -- normalized to map image, 0..1
  w REAL NOT NULL, h REAL NOT NULL,
  sort INTEGER NOT NULL
)
```

- Partial unique index ensures exactly one draft.
- Schema version tracked with `PRAGMA user_version`; migration hook prepared for later changes.
- Map image stored outside the DB under `QStandardPaths::AppDataLocation/maps/property.png`.
- Rectangles are normalized so the saved image resolution can change later.

## Map setup flow

1. First run shows `MapSetupPage` because no `map` row exists.
2. User enters an address, presses Search.
3. `Geocoder` queries Nominatim (`/search?format=jsonv2`), with identifiable User-Agent and throttling. Multiple results are shown for selection; manual lat/lon fallback is available if search fails.
4. Map centers on the chosen result. `MapCanvas`:
   - renders OSM tiles at a zoom targeting **~70 m across ≈ 1 acre** around the crosshair,
   - supports drag-to-pan only; scale stays fixed,
   - requires all tiles loaded before OK is enabled.
5. OK captures the square canvas at ~768×768 with attribution already rendered into the image, writes it atomically, saves the `map` row, creates an empty draft, and switches to the main page.
6. Once saved, the map is displayed only as the fixed local image; no tile network access is needed during daily use.
7. The map cannot be replaced after setup in the first version. This avoids silently misaligning existing records.

## Main window behavior

Layout: record list on the left, square fixed map in the center, editor/details on the right. A toolbar shows the property address and context actions.

### Edit mode (draft)
- Starting the app always loads the draft and enters edit mode, even if the draft is partially filled.
- Drag on the map to create rectangles. Multiple rectangles supported.
- Existing rectangles can be selected, moved, resized, and deleted.
- Editor fields: notes, date (ISO text field + calendar popup, default today), tag (with suggestions from existing tags), color picker.
- All field/rectangle changes are persisted immediately to SQLite. A small “Saved” indicator confirms persistence.
- **Commit** validates a valid date, non-empty tag, and at least one rectangle; commits in one transaction, creates a new empty draft, refreshes the list, and selects the new record.

### Viewing a committed record
- Selecting a list item flushes the draft first, then exits edit mode and shows that record’s rectangles and read-only details.
- The draft remains untouched in the database.
- A persistent banner/button **Resume editing** returns to the draft.
- **Clear draft** asks for confirmation, deletes draft rectangles, resets fields to defaults, and returns to an empty edit session.
- The record list is sorted by `date DESC, created_at DESC`.

## Map rendering details

- `TileImageProvider` uses an async `QQuickAsyncImageProvider`, an identifying User-Agent, and a disk cache under `QStandardPaths::CacheLocation/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`.
- Tile configuration is centralized (`urlTemplate`, attribution, min/max zoom) so satellite tiles can be added later.
- Zoom is computed from latitude and target ground span; tiles are scaled smoothly when the required zoom exceeds OSM’s max.
- Crosshair is UI-only and excluded from the captured image; attribution is included.
- On-screen map area is forced square to keep normalized rectangle coordinates exact.
- If `grabToImage` proves unreliable, fallback is to compose the saved image in C++ from the same cached tiles using `QPainter`.

## Implementation phases

1. **Scaffold**
   - CMake project with `qt_add_qml_module`, Qt 6.12, executable + module.
   - Database class, schema creation, models, `AppStore` skeleton.
   - Basic empty ApplicationWindow builds and launches.

2. **Persistence and application state**
   - Draft create/load/update/clear, commit transaction, record ordering.
   - Rectangle CRUD and normalized-coordinate conversion.
   - Unit tests for draft persistence, commit, ordering, cascade deletion.

3. **Map setup**
   - Tile provider with caching and UA.
   - MapCanvas pan/zoom/crosshair and tile-ready detection.
   - Nominatim geocoder and address results UI.
   - Map image capture and `map` persistence.

4. **Main map and records**
   - Fixed map display, rectangle overlays, record list, record selection/details.
   - Resume editing / draft restore behavior.

5. **Draft editor**
   - Draw/move/resize/delete rectangles.
   - Notes/date/tag/color fields with immediate autosave.
   - Commit validation and clear-draft confirmation.

6. **Polish and verification**
   - Attribution, error/empty states, keyboard delete, window sizing.
   - Startup always shows draft; navigation flushes pending edits.
   - Run `qmllint`, unit tests, and a manual end-to-end checklist.

## Build and test commands

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/home/dwight/Qt/6.12.0/gcc_64 \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
./build/poisonlog
```

## Risks / mitigations
- **Nominatim/OSM usage policy:** proper User-Agent, throttling, attribution, no bulk prefetching.
- **OSM resolution at ~1 acre:** OSM max zoom yields a modest source resolution; stored image is upscaled slightly. The pluggable provider supports satellite/high-zoom later.
- **Network only during setup:** all daily work uses the saved image and local SQLite.
- **Draft loss:** immediate writes plus flush before any navigation and on window close.
- **Rectangle alignment:** square fixed image and normalized coordinates avoid resize/layout drift.

## Out of scope for first version
Multiple properties, editing committed records, record deletion, cloud sync, and satellite provider credentials/UI.

--- qml/MapCanvas.qml	
+++ qml/MapCanvas.qml	
@@ -0,0 +1,172 @@
+import QtQuick
+
+Item {
+    id: root
+    clip: true
+
+    property real centerLat: 0
+    property real centerLon: 0
+    property real groundSpanMeters: 70
+    property string attribution: "© OpenStreetMap contributors"
+    property bool active: true
+
+    readonly property real effectiveZoom: {
+        const mppAtZoomZero = 156543.03392 * Math.cos(centerLat * Math.PI / 180)
+        return Math.log(Math.max(1e-9, mppAtZoomZero * Math.max(width, 1) / groundSpanMeters))
+            / Math.LN2
+    }
+    readonly property int tileZoom: Math.max(1, Math.min(19, Math.floor(effectiveZoom)))
+    readonly property real tileScale: Math.pow(2, effectiveZoom - tileZoom)
+    readonly property real tileDisplaySize: 256 * tileScale
+    readonly property real centerWorldX: lonToWorldX(centerLon, effectiveZoom)
+    readonly property real centerWorldY: latToWorldY(centerLat, effectiveZoom)
+    readonly property var tileItems: computeTiles()
+    property bool tilesReady: false
+
+    function normalizeLon(lon) {
+        return ((lon + 180) % 360 + 360) % 360 - 180
+    }
+
+    function lonToWorldX(lon, zoom) {
+        return (normalizeLon(lon) + 180) / 360 * 256 * Math.pow(2, zoom)
+    }
+
+    function latToWorldY(lat, zoom) {
+        const clamped = Math.max(-85.05112878, Math.min(85.05112878, lat))
+        const radians = clamped * Math.PI / 180
+        return (1 - Math.log(Math.tan(radians) + 1 / Math.cos(radians)) / Math.PI)
+            / 2 * 256 * Math.pow(2, zoom)
+    }
+
+    function computeTiles() {
+        if (!active || width <= 0 || height <= 0 || !isFinite(effectiveZoom))
+            return []
+
+        const zoom = tileZoom
+        const scale = tileScale
+        const centerX = lonToWorldX(centerLon, zoom)
+        const centerY = latToWorldY(centerLat, zoom)
+        const halfWidth = (width / 2) / scale
+        const halfHeight = (height / 2) / scale
+        const minX = Math.floor((centerX - halfWidth) / 256)
+        const maxX = Math.floor((centerX + halfWidth) / 256)
+        const minY = Math.floor((centerY - halfHeight) / 256)
+        const maxY = Math.floor((centerY + halfHeight) / 256)
+        const tileCount = 1 << zoom
+        const result = []
+
+        for (let tileY = minY; tileY <= maxY; ++tileY) {
+            if (tileY < 0 || tileY >= tileCount)
+                continue
+            for (let tileX = minX; tileX <= maxX; ++tileX) {
+                const sourceX = ((tileX % tileCount) + tileCount) % tileCount
+                result.push({
+                    sourceX: sourceX,
+                    tileY: tileY,
+                    x: (tileX * 256 - centerX) * scale + width / 2,
+                    y: (tileY * 256 - centerY) * scale + height / 2
+                })
+            }
+        }
+        return result
+    }
+
+    function panBy(dx, dy) {
+        if (!active || width <= 0 || height <= 0)
+            return
+
+        const zoom = effectiveZoom
+        const worldPixels = 256 * Math.pow(2, zoom)
+        const centerX = lonToWorldX(centerLon, zoom) - dx * worldPixels / width
+        const centerY = latToWorldY(centerLat, zoom) - dy * worldPixels / height
+        const newLon = normalizeLon(centerX / worldPixels * 360 - 180)
+        const mercatorY = Math.PI - 2 * Math.PI * centerY / worldPixels
+        const newLat = Math.atan(Math.sinh(mercatorY)) * 180 / Math.PI
+
+        centerLat = Math.max(-85, Math.min(85, newLat))
+        centerLon = newLon
+    }
+
+    function evaluateTileReadiness() {
+        let ready = repeater.count > 0
+        for (let i = 0; i < repeater.count; ++i) {
+            const image = repeater.itemAt(i)
+            if (!image || image["status"] !== Image.Ready) {
+                ready = false
+                break
+            }
+        }
+        if (tilesReady !== ready)
+            tilesReady = ready
+    }
+
+    onTileItemsChanged: tilesReady = false
+
+    Repeater {
+        id: repeater
+        model: root.tileItems
+        delegate: Image {
+            required property var modelData
+
+            x: modelData.x
+            y: modelData.y
+            width: root.tileDisplaySize
+            height: root.tileDisplaySize
+            source: root.active
+                ? "image://tiles/" + root.tileZoom + "/" + modelData.sourceX + "/" + modelData.tileY
+                : ""
+            fillMode: Image.Stretch
+            asynchronous: true
+            cache: true
+            smooth: true
+        }
+    }
+
+    MouseArea {
+        anchors.fill: parent
+        enabled: root.active
+        acceptedButtons: Qt.LeftButton
+        cursorShape: Qt.ClosedHandCursor
+
+        property real lastX: 0
+        property real lastY: 0
+
+        onPressed: (mouse) => {
+            lastX = mouse.x
+            lastY = mouse.y
+        }
+        onPositionChanged: (mouse) => {
+            if (!pressed)
+                return
+            root.panBy(mouse.x - lastX, mouse.y - lastY)
+            lastX = mouse.x
+            lastY = mouse.y
+        }
+    }
+
+    Timer {
+        interval: 80
+        repeat: true
+        running: root.active
+        onTriggered: root.evaluateTileReadiness()
+    }
+
+    Rectangle {
+        z: 10
+        anchors.right: parent.right
+        anchors.bottom: parent.bottom
+        anchors.margins: 4
+        width: attributionText.implicitWidth + 10
+        height: attributionText.implicitHeight + 4
+        radius: 2
+        color: "#e6ffffff"
+
+        Text {
+            id: attributionText
+            anchors.centerIn: parent
+            text: root.attribution
+            font.pixelSize: 10
+            color: "#304437"
+        }
+    }
+}

parts.text:
FDs 575 after one 5.6s pan, threads 182! This is leak. Threads from QNetworkAccessManager each creates? Each QNAM has connection thread? 182 threads huge. So per-tile QNAM is disaster. Need redesign with shared QNAM in dedicated thread or in provider? We avoided GUI thread issue. We can use a single QNetworkAccessManager living in a dedicated worker thread, with requests dispatched to it, then reply image loaded and response finished on provider thread? Need understand QQuickAsyncImageProvider: requestImageResponse called on QQuickPixmapReader thread (not GUI), responses should use that thread. We can create a long-lived QNetworkAccessManager per provider on the pixmap reader thread? But provider is global; requestImageResponse runs on a single thread? QQuickPixmapReader uses a separate thread, likely one. We could lazily create QNAM in requestImageResponse (thus first call on reader thread), store as member, reusing. It would be used only on that thread (assuming all requestImageResponse calls from same thread). Is QQuickPixmapReader one thread? Yes, QQuickPixmapReader is a QThread; all async image requests happen there. But to be safe, use a worker thread with one QNAM and per-request signal.

Simplest robust design:
- TileImageProvider holds `QNetworkAccessManager *m_network` created lazily via QThreadStorage? Or ensure by thread check? Since provider lives GUI but method on reader thread, we can use `QThreadStorage<QNetworkAccessManager*>` but then one per thread, and cleanup. But thread may be long-lived; one QNAM should be fine. Yet current problem includes creating QNAM per response and threads 182. Reusing one per thread fixes FD/thread leak.
- Need handle cancellation without aborting shared cache? If QML destroys image (delegate destroyed), response cancel should abort its reply. With one shared QNAM, abort reply and deleteLater. But repeated panning creates new request for same tile; can use shared in-flight dedup; not necessary but good.
- Even with one QNAM, rapid panning destroys/creates tiles and issues many requests due delegate rebuild. Network connections may accumulate if no reuse? One QNAM uses connection pooling, so at most 6 connections. FDs stable. Threads? QNAM with HTTP/2 may spawn threads? One QNAM likely few.
- Better to prevent unnecessary request churn and make panning smooth: don't rebuild Repeater delegates each pan. Use a fixed grid of tiles or use Canvas. But the immediate crash/FD exhaustion can be fixed by QNAM reuse. Also tile images blank due "Out of resources" from FD exhaustion. Clicking/panning triggered more and then crash.

Why FD count starts 229, after search 253, after pan 575; threads 182. Yes each QNAM creates 1-2 threads. Need fix.

The user says "tiles show nothing" before drag? Maybe their cache or network issue; but our reproduction shows tiles. Could be on their first attempt the network/FD issue caused "Out of resources" after a minute; maybe screenshot they saw blank due tile images not rendering because texture resource exhaustion from leaked QNAMs? The output "Map tile download failed: Out of resources" likely socket creation failed due FD/threads. Fixing QNAM should resolve.

Also the "clicking on map changes how it appears" may be because each pan triggers many delegate rebuilds and eventually some tiles appear differently. We can improve design to avoid full Repeater rebuild by changing tile model.

Let's inspect user build: their CMake compiled old code. We'll fix and rebuild both `build` and Qt Creator's `build/Desktop_Qt_6_12_0-Debug` perhaps by invoking its build script? User can rebuild. But we should test actual app from our build path maybe use existing Qt Creator build? We can build both with cmake --build. Need perhaps not modify their build? It's fine to rebuild after source change. But final we tell rerun.

Design tile provider with shared QNAM. Options:

A) Provider owns QNetworkAccessManager created in reader thread on first request:
```
QNetworkAccessManager *networkManager() {
  QThread *current = QThread::currentThread();
  if (!m_network) { m_network = new QNetworkAccessManager; m_network->moveToThread(current); }
  Q_ASSERT(m_network->thread() == current);
  ...
}
```
Provider destructor? Response may outlive provider? Engine destroys provider after QML; responses maybe. Use QPointer? Not. Could parent QNAM to provider but provider in GUI thread, object affinity to reader thread; child QNAM destroyed when provider deleted from GUI thread would be wrong. Set parent nullptr and provider destructor post delete to its thread? During shutdown maybe.

B) Dedicated worker `TileNetwork` QObject + QThread. Requests:
  - TileImageResponse constructed on pixmap reader thread. It sends request to worker via queued signal, worker does QNAM get. On reply finished, worker reads data and emits `finished(id, QByteArray, error)`. Response receives on reader thread, decodes image, caches, saves, emits finished.
  - Cancellation: response emits cancelRequest(reply pointer/id, token) queued; worker aborts and deletes. Need avoid races.
  - Dedup? optional.
  - QNAM lives entirely worker thread. One thread + one QNAM. FDs bounded.
  - Provider owns worker thread and singleton network manager. Lifecycle okay: provider created in main; worker start; destructor stops thread. Responses are children? QQuickPixmapReader manages responses; if provider destroyed, pending responses? app shutting down; fine. But worker signals to deleted response safe via QObject connections; provider destructor stops worker potentially while response waiting. Not issue.

C) Keep QNAM per response but use `QNetworkAccessManager` without per-request threads? QNAM can spawn threads due HTTP2? 182 threads for ~100 QNAMs suggests each has 1 thread plus event? Shared QNAM best.

Simplest shared per reader thread (A) likely enough and less code. But robust with dedicated worker maybe overkill. QQuickPixmapReader's thread should be unique. Yet shared QNAM must be destroyed in correct thread. We could make QNAM a child of a QObject created with no parent, and connect provider destroyed? We can just leak one QNAM at app exit? Not ideal but one object. Or use thread-local storage:

Need test save map at actual app. Since crosshair and tiles ready, Save map should work. Click save at 1330,843. Then main view; then drag rectangle and see if crash. Also test save.

input.command:
W=69206034; P=$(cat /tmp/poisonlog-repro4/pid)
xdotool mousemove --window $W 1330 843 click 1
sleep 4
echo "after save fds=$(lsof -p $P 2>/dev/null | wc -l) threads=$(ls /proc/$P/task | wc -l)"; import -window $W /tmp/poisonlog-repro4/main-after-save.png; find /tmp/poisonlog-repro4 -type f | sort; tail -5 /tmp/poisonlog-repro4/log.txt

USGS Imagery Only is a tile cache base map service of orthoimagery in The National Map visible to the 1:9,028 zoom scale. Orthoimagery data are typically high resolution aerial images that combine the visual attributes of an aerial photograph with the spatial accuracy and reliability of a planimetric map. USGS digital orthoimage resolution may vary from 6 inches to 1 meter. In the former resolution, every pixel in an orthoimage covers a six inch square of the earth's surface, while in the latter resolution, one meter square is represented by each pixel. Blue Marble: Next Generation and Landsat imagery data sources are displayed at small to medium scales, however, the majority of the imagery service source is from the National Agriculture Imagery Program (NAIP) for the conterminous United States. The data is 1 meter pixel resolution collected with 'leaf-on' conditions. Collection of NAIP imagery is administered by the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Farm Service Agency (FSA). In areas where NAIP data is not available, other imagery may be acquired through partnerships by the USGS. For Alaska, 10-meter resolution SPOT imagery is provided for viewing. The National Map download client allows free downloads of public domain, 1-meter resolution orthoimagery in JPEG 2000 (jp2) format for the conterminous United States.  However, the 10-meter Alaska orthoimagery data will not be available for direct download from the National Map due to license restrictions. For additional information on orthoimagery, go to https://nationalmap.gov/ortho.html.NAIP Data is from 2017-2021 for CONUS, 2013 and 2020 for HI and AK respectively, PR - 2018, and 2012-2013 for the Territories.
